meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm here.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: What are you doing?
I'm making dinner.
Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?
As you all know...
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.trans: The court has decided.
I've decided.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'vegetarian' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a strict vegetarian.

examples.text: Вегетарианцы — это люди, которые не едят мясо.
examples.trans: Vegetarians are people who do not eat meat.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('normal').

examples.trans: It's a decent job.
Normal jokes.
Normal jokes. Where's the money?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'food, meal' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Oh, bad food?

examples.text: В этом ресторане всегда свежая еда.
examples.trans: There is always fresh food in this restaurant.
Oh no, bad food? Does your stomach hurt?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to feed', paired with 'накормить'.

examples.trans: The cook feeds the guests a delicious lunch.

examples.text: Быстро беги на кухню и корми людей!
examples.trans: Quickly run to the kitchen and feed people!

examples.text: Ты кормишь рыбу лучше наших гостей.
examples.trans: You feed the fish better than our guests.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'meat' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Where do you get your meat?
Very tasty meat!

examples.text: И мой тоже готов! А ты где мясо берёшь?
examples.trans: And mine is ready too! Where do you get your meat?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

examples.text: Хорошо. Значит, вот куда идут деньги налогоплательщиков.
examples.trans: Fine. So this is where taxpayers' money goes.

examples.text: Значит, вот куда идут деньги налогоплательщиков.
examples.trans: So this is where taxpayers' money goes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, it's mine.
No? All right.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: А ты иди на биржу труда. Там есть работа.
examples.trans: You go to the job centre. There's work there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

ездить.gloss: to go (by vehicle, regularly), to drive

meanings.en: to go (by vehicle, regularly), to drive
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle, regularly), to drive'.

examples.text: Послушайте, Артурик, я уже давно не танцую. И в сауну я не езжу.
examples.trans: Listen, Arturik, I haven't danced in a long time. And I don't go to saunas.
We drive Russian cars.
He often goes to Moscow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to panic'.

examples.trans: Do not panic ahead of time.

examples.text: Вика, не паникуй, я уже несу горячее блюдо.
examples.trans: Vika, do not panic, I am already carrying the hot dish.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'even', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Even a child knows.
Even Mum doesn't know.
Yes! Even a child knows.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'метить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to notice, spot', paired with 'замечать'.

examples.trans: He did not notice the loss.

examples.text: Никто на кухне ничего не заметил.
examples.trans: Nobody in the kitchen noticed anything.
And what if someone notices me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I don't know anything.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.
How are things?

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!
Thank you for your trust!

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('agreeing; consonant').

examples.trans: I agree.

examples.text: Я их продам и куплю тебе приставку. Ну, согласен?
examples.trans: I'll sell it and buy you a console. Well, deal?
Well, we agree!

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('vegetarian').

examples.trans: Agreed, vegetarians are total idiots too.

examples.text: Скажите, а нет ли у вас чего-нибудь вегетарианского?
examples.trans: Tell me, do you have anything vegetarian?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'idiot, fool' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Do you take me for an idiot?

examples.text: У вас даже синяка нет. Вы меня за идиота держите?
examples.trans: You don't even have a bruise. Do you take me for an idiot?

examples.text: Боже мой! Какой же я идиот!
examples.trans: My goodness! What an idiot I am!
